title: Orientation
source: Rector, PEN&PAD, GALEN & GRAIL, DRAFT Nov 2026, p. 1.

steps.title: Search
steps.body: The box in the top bar opens a concept by its OpenGALEN name. Thumb is open. The heading joins equivalent names: Thumb = Pollux. One node, both names.
steps.task: Type thumb and choose Thumb, or leave the concept this step opened.

quote.text: Sound, Computable, Human comprehensible – i.e. capable of being presented so as to be understood and used by end users and developers.

steps.note: The draft’s stated goal was “Useful and Usable systems for health care professionals.” Terminology and concept modelling were “a means to that end.” (p. 1).

steps.title: The graph
steps.body: Ancestors sit above the focus and children below. A dashed +n pill is a cluster of intermediate ancestors. Click the pill to expand it. Click a node to make it the focus.
steps.task: Click a +n pill, or click a node.

steps.title: The side panel
steps.body: The side panel is the detail for the focus: the definition, parents, children, and the other lists. Thumb and Pollux share this node. The address keeps the name you opened.
steps.task: Read the heading and the Parents list. Finger is a parent of this concept.

steps.title: Clustering
steps.body: Clustering, beside the search box, folds intermediate ancestors into +n pills. Turn it off and every ancestor is its own node. Children, in the side panel, shows or hides concepts directly under the focus. It starts on.
steps.task: Turn Clustering off, then on again.

steps.title: The address, and a red link
steps.body: The address of this concept is #concept=first. The red is-a link up to OrdinalPositionValueType is a told OWL SubClassOf parent that the published classified dump omitted. This page restores it from the source. It does not run a classifier. The banner points at issue #10. Incoming relationships list concepts whose definitions use first, including Thumb = Pollux with hasOrdinalPosition.
steps.task: Look at the red link or the word “told” beside the parent. Then open Incoming relationships in the side panel.
